answer: A staking economy resists Sybil attacks by making identity costly: each agent locks a bond, and voting weight is the square root of locked stake, not stake itself. An attacker splitting capital across a mirror army of fake wallets gains no edge, since weight per identity shrinks. Climbing the influence ridge means posting a bond that scales with the horizon of ambition: to rival honest voters, one must lock capital near the whole honest pool, and caught equivocation slashes it. Splitting burns money, buying no power.
